# `m.options.last_trade`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

The latest trade of each US-listed options contract.

```python
m.options.last_trade(symbols)
```

[All datasets](README.md)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Verbs | `fetch()`, `poll()` |
| Served by | REST |
| `poll()` | `dm.PollMode.REPLACE`: holds exactly the latest cycle's rows, keyed by `Symbol`; `mode=dm.PollMode.APPEND` also keys by `Timestamp` |

## Plan access

Which of Massive's plans include this dataset, how recent its data is on each, and how far back its history goes, as Massive's pages state them.

| Plan | Last Trade (REST) |
| --- | --- |
| Options Basic | Not included |
| Options Starter | Not included |
| Options Developer | 15-minute delayed |
| Options Advanced | Real-time |
| Options Business | Not included |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The instrument, in the library's canonical symbol form. From REST `T`: "The exchange symbol that this item is traded under." | REST |
| `Date` | String | The trading day of the row, as ISO yyyy-MM-dd text: the New York date of `Timestamp`. | REST |
| `Timestamp` | Instant | The row's primary time, as an Instant. From REST `t`: "The nanosecond accuracy SIP Unix Timestamp. This is the timestamp of when the SIP received this message from the exchange which produced it." | REST |
| `OptionRoot` | String | The OCC option root, read from `Symbol`: the symbol without its `O:` prefix and its last 15 characters (expiry, type, and strike), such as `SPXW` for `O:SPXW251219C06000000`. It is never mapped to the underlying: an adjusted contract keeps its own root, such as `AAPL1`. | REST |
| `RawSymbol` | String | The symbol exactly as Massive sent it, on a row whose spelling the library cannot read as the dataset's class (its `Symbol` is then null); null on every other row. Present unless the session's `unreadable_symbols` is `dm.OnError.RAISE`, which fails on such a row instead. | REST |
| `Price` | double | The price of the trade. This is the price per share of the underlying, so the total dollar value of a trade is the price multiplied by the size and by the contract multiplier, which is typically 100 shares per contract. | REST |
| `Size` | double | The size of a trade (also known as volume). | REST |
| `Conditions` | long[] | A list of condition codes. See Options Condition Codes (https://massive.com/docs/rest/options/market-operations/condition-codes) for what each code means. | REST |
| `Correction` | long | The trade correction indicator. | REST |
| `Exchange` | long | The exchange ID. See Exchanges (https://massive.com/docs/rest/options/market-operations/exchanges) for Massive's mapping of exchange IDs. | REST |
| `Id` | String | The trade ID. Options trades do not have a trade ID, so this field is returned as an empty string. | REST |
| `ParticipantTimestamp` | Instant | The nanosecond accuracy Participant/Exchange Unix Timestamp. This is the timestamp of when the trade was actually generated at the exchange. | REST |
| `SequenceNumber` | long | The sequence number represents the sequence in which message events happened. These are increasing and unique per ticker symbol, but will not always be sequential (e.g., 1, 2, 6, 9, 10, 11). | REST |
| `Tape` | long | There are 3 tapes which define which exchange the ticker is listed on. These are integers in our objects which represent the letter of the alphabet. Eg: 1 = A, 2 = B, 3 = C. * Tape A is NYSE listed securities * Tape B is NYSE ARCA / NYSE American * Tape C is NASDAQ | REST |
| `TrfId` | long | The ID for the Trade Reporting Facility where the trade took place. | REST |
| `TrfTimestamp` | Instant | The nanosecond accuracy TRF(Trade Reporting Facility) Unix Timestamp. This is the timestamp of when the trade reporting facility received this message. | REST |
| `DecimalSize` | String | The size of the trade including the fractional component. This is represented as a decimal string. | REST |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST |
